quote: Before going into the details, let us recall one important general family of distributions. We say that random variable X belongs to the Exponentiated Scale (ES) family of distributions if X ∼ H(x) = [G(λx)]^α, where α, λ > 0 and G is called the baseline distribution function which we assume that is absolutely continuous. In the sequel, we denote this family by ES(α, λ). Bashkar et al. (2017) proved the following general result. Theorem 11. Suppose for i = 1, ..., n, X_i ∼ ES(α_i, λ) and X*_i ∼ ES(α*_i, λ) share a common Archimedean survival copula with generator ϕ. Then, X_{1:n} ≤_st X*_{1:n} if (α_1, ..., α_n) ⪰^w (α*_1, ..., α*_n).
